description:
Composite-chart wheel from two natal inputs. Computes midpoint composite then renders as Western wheel.

[Group: Visualization]
[Endpoint: POST /v1/render/composite]
[Cost: 10 credits (Tier 1)]

allOf.description: Pair of natal charts for relationship calculations: synastry, composite, davison.

chart1.description: Birth data for a single natal chart. Required: date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:mm:ss), latitude and longitude in decimal degrees. The short forms lat, lon, lng and tz are rejected with 400 INVALID_FIELD; pass the full names. timezoneOffset is hours from UTC and defaults to 0, meaning UTC; send timezone instead (an IANA name such as Europe/Kyiv, or auto) and the offset for that date is worked out, summer time included. city is a display label only: nothing here geocodes it, so it never stands in for coordinates. houseSystem is a single house-system letter, P by default; a name such as "Placidus" is refused, and the case matters because I and i are two different Sunshine systems.

ayanamsa.description: Sidereal school by name. Lahiri when omitted. Equivalent to ayanamsaId; send either.

timezone.description: IANA zone name such as Europe/Kyiv, or auto to look the zone up from latitude and longitude. The server takes the offset that zone kept at this local date and time, summer time included, and uses it in place of timezoneOffset. A clock time that happened twice takes the first occurrence; one skipped when clocks went forward takes the offset from before the change. Abbreviations such as EST are refused. Before 1970 the tz database is not reliable for every place, so send timezoneOffset when the local clock is known.

timezoneOffset.description: Hours from UTC at the given moment, not minutes. Fractional zones are hours too: 5.5 for India, 5.75 for Nepal, -3.5 for Newfoundland. Defaults to 0, meaning UTC. Ignored when timezone is sent.

labels.description: Your own words in place of the English the image would otherwise carry: the ASC/DSC/MC/IC axis labels, the SVG <title> and <desc> read by screen readers, and the planet and sign names plus the word for retrograde in each planet's data-label (theme css). bodies is keyed by the English name, signs lists twelve names from Aries. Nothing is translated for you; absent keys keep the English.

theme.description: css paints every colour as var(--aw-, ), so the page that inlines the SVG can recolour it with CSS custom properties (--aw-chart-bg, --aw-fg, --aw-muted, --aw-ring, --aw-houses-fill, --aw-benefic, --aw-malefic, --aw-aspect-harmonious, --aw-aspect-tense, --aw-aspect-neutral, --aw-aspect-minor, --aw-aspect-quintile, --aw-moon-shadow, --aw-moon-light, --aw-cycle-physical, --aw-cycle-emotional, --aw-cycle-intellectual). With none set it looks exactly like light. Inside an the variables cannot be set, so it stays light. The Western wheels and the aspect grid then also carry stable aw-* classes, and each planet is a with data-planet and data-label, each aspect line has data-a and data-b; see the @astroway/render changelog for the list.
